title: skills sync reports a conflict for skills whose canon and installed trees are byte-identical
body:
**`intent claude skills sync` reports `changed upstream AND here -- HELD` for three skills whose canon and installed trees are BYTE-IDENTICAL, and the message it prints tells the operator that forcing will discard their work.** There is provably nothing to discard. Measured 2026-09-08.

**THE THREE CHECKSUMS, COMPUTED WITH `payload.rs`'s OWN ALGORITHM** (relative path + NUL + sha256(content) + LF, over the whole tree, `checksum_scope: tree` as the live manifest declares):

| skill | canon | installed | manifest | canon==installed | verdict printed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `in-tca-audit` | `262b9722` | `262b9722` | `5bc75387` | **TRUE** | HELD |
| `in-tca-finish` | `5254cb07` | `5254cb07` | `2cc0689f` | **TRUE** | HELD |
| `in-tca-init` | `d480f44f` | `d480f44f` | `fc70bb78` | **TRUE** | HELD |
| `in-standards` | `220f7d20` | `eb042d76` | `eb042d76` | false | `updated` -- CORRECT |
| `in-detrope` | `60a1dc29` | `60a1dc29` | `60a1dc29` | true | `up to date` -- CORRECT |

**THE MECHANISM,** confirmed by cc against `payload.rs:1006-1012`: `source_moved = old != source`, `target_moved = old != target`, **each side against the MANIFEST and never against each other.** Both limbs are true for the three above only because the manifest baseline records neither side.

**CORRECTION, cc's, 2026-09-08: this issue first dated those baselines `recorded 2026-04-28` off the `installed_at` field. That field is `mtime_rfc3339(installed_marker)` -- the FILE's mtime, not when the row was written -- so the manifest does not state when it was recorded and my sentence claimed it did.** The diagnosis is untouched; the provenance claim was mine and was wrong.

**AND THE ROOT IS A LATCH, WHICH THIS ISSUE ORIGINALLY LEFT UNMEASURED AND cc SETTLED.** No held outcome calls `manifest.upsert` -- correctly, since nothing was written -- **so the stale baseline that causes the hold survives the run that reports it, and every later sync recomputes the same verdict forever. Held because stale, stale because held.** Driven, not hypothesised: the manifest's own mtime is later than the rows it holds, so sync has run since these went stale and left all four untouched. **What wrote the installed trees without recording, around 2026-08-30, is still unidentified** -- not in the Rust source, the templates or `bin/`. **When canon and installed agree, there is no conflict to resolve whatever the baseline says; both sides are the same bytes.** The honest verdict is *up to date, baseline refreshed*, not *needs a decision*. The two correct rows above show the logic works whenever the manifest is current, so this is a missing case rather than a broken comparison.

**`in-essentials` IS THE FOURTH HELD ROW AND ITS `changed here` LIMB IS ALSO FALSE.** Its installed tree is byte-identical to canon at `HEAD~1` -- diffed, empty -- so it carries no local edit; it matches a PRIOR canon while the manifest (recorded `2026-08-25`) records neither. Same root: **the manifest is not a reliable record of what is installed, and the whole conflict verdict rests on it.**

**WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A COSMETIC WRONG VERDICT.** The message reads *`--force` takes the source copy and reports the checksum of what it discarded; copy your edits out first if you want them*. An operator who believes it will decline to force, correctly, on the evidence in front of them -- and the skill then stays stale permanently. **The safe reading and the correct action point in opposite directions.**

**AND IT LANDS ON THE ONE PATH THAT MATTERS FOR `ST0056 AC-15.3`**, which requires that a change carried out through `intent claude skills` REACHES a consumer, asserted by driving a consumer install. A correction landed in canon today (`20841a5e8`, striking a frontmatter format v3 has never written, in `in-essentials` -- the skill `/in-session` loads every session) cannot reach any consumer on this machine except by overriding a warning that falsely implies data loss. **4 of 23 skills are in this state.**

**FIXED BY cc AT `b31ecbc7f`**, as the missing case this issue argued it was: `payload.rs` already carried the rebaselining argument for `old == None` -- *the objection is that it discards the distinction between an upstream change and a local edit; here there is no distinction to discard* -- reachable only when NO baseline existed. A merely STALE baseline is the same situation and now takes the same arm. Dry-run on the live state: **four needing a decision becomes one.**

**THE ONE THAT REMAINS IS `in-essentials`, AND IT IS CORRECTLY HELD.** Its canon and installed trees genuinely differ, because canon moved in `20841a5e8` today. **With the baseline matching neither side, that signature is IDENTICAL to a genuine conflict** -- `old` described the tree at install time and both sides then moved -- so nothing in the manifest can separate them. It was proved not-an-edit by diffing installed against canon at `HEAD~1`; `payload.rs` has no git history and cannot do that.

**cc CONSIDERED REPORTING `Undecidable` FOR A BASELINE MATCHING NEITHER SIDE AND DROPPED IT, WHICH IS THE BEST JUDGEMENT ON THIS ISSUE:** a real conflict produces that same signature, so the change would have relabelled genuine conflicts as undecidable -- a confident wrong fix that was one measurement away from looking obviously right.

**WHAT IS LEFT IS THE STRING, NOT THE VERDICT.** The remedy for `in-essentials` is `--force` and it is correct in substance; the message tells the operator it will discard work that has not been shown to exist. *Changed here* is not established when the baseline records neither side. An operator-facing wording on a destructive remedy is a validation call and is recorded here rather than taken silently.

Reported by vc; routed to cc, who owns `payload.rs`'s neighbourhood and was idle. Corroborates from a third angle that skills are tree-scoped in v3: the live manifest's own `checksum_scope` field reads `tree`.
